entries.use_case: Inside Kilo, add an MCP server or mode from the marketplace instead of hand-editing config.
entries.safety_notes: Company repo; hits are a skill that refuses to collect secrets in chat and a policy file that blocks credential paths

entries.name: Sentry skills
entries.author: Sentry
entries.description: The skills Sentry's own engineers use for development work (code review, commits, PR writing, security review), shared in the open. Good examples of practical team skills; for Sentry setup itself, see sentry-for-ai. Install with the Claude marketplace or `npx skills add getsentry/skills`.
entries.use_case: Have the agent write a PR description and run a security review using the same skills Sentry's engineers use.
entries.safety_notes: Official; all exfil and base64 hits are documented attack examples

entries.name: 12-Factor Agents
entries.author: Dex Horthy (HumanLayer)
entries.description: Dex Horthy's essay-style guide to 12 principles for reliable LLM applications (own your prompts, own your context window, small focused agents and so on). Not a tool, but widely cited for agent product design. Read it on GitHub.
entries.use_case: Before designing a production agent, read the 12 principles and check your architecture owns its prompts, context and control flow.
entries.safety_notes: Docs only

entries.name: claude-mem
entries.author: Alex Newman (thedotmack)
entries.description: Claude-Mem records your coding sessions and gives the agent searchable memory across sessions, with compressed summaries. Useful if you lose context between sessions often. Install with `npx claude-mem install`; analytics are on by default.
entries.use_case: Pick up yesterday's debugging session and have the agent recall which fixes it already tried, without re-explaining.
entries.safety_notes: Records full sessions; anonymous analytics on by default (opt out with its telemetry command)

entries.name: Hugging Face skills
entries.author: Hugging Face
entries.description: Hugging Face's skills for ML work on the Hub: an hf-cli bootstrap skill plus dataset creation, model training and evaluation workflows. Useful when you fine-tune, evaluate or host models. Add via plugin marketplaces or `hf skills add`.
entries.use_case: Have the agent create a dataset on the Hub, fine-tune a small model on it and run an evaluation.
entries.safety_notes: Official; installs HF CLI from hf.co

entries.name: Langfuse skills
entries.author: Langfuse
entries.description: Agent Skills that teach a coding agent to add Langfuse tracing, prompt management and evals to your app correctly. Copy them in when wiring Langfuse into an agent product.
entries.use_case: Have the agent add Langfuse tracing and prompt management to your app correctly on the first try.
entries.safety_notes: Official Langfuse; docs; keys via env

entries.name: wshobson agents
entries.author: Seth Hobson
entries.description: A very large collection of plugins, subagents, skills and commands written once in Claude Code format, with adapters that generate versions for Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Copilot and Pi. Useful as a menu of specialist agents (languages, infra, security). Add it as a Claude marketplace and install only the plugins you read.
entries.use_case: Install just the Python-testing or Kubernetes specialist subagent from the catalog when a task needs that expertise.
entries.safety_notes: Very large community set; some plugins hook every tool call. Install only the plugins you read

entries.name: Claude Code Templates
entries.author: Daniel Avila
entries.description: A big catalog of Claude Code components (skills, subagents, commands, hooks, MCP configs, settings) installable with one command, plus a browsing site. Good for quick experiments; contents are community-contributed. Run `npx claude-code-templates@latest`.
entries.use_case: Try a ready-made status line or hook config for Claude Code in one command, then keep or delete it.
entries.safety_notes: Huge community set, including offensive-security skills; vet each one
entries.related_note: Re-bundles skills from Anthropic, OpenAI and Composio lists

entries.name: dbt MCP
entries.author: dbt Labs
entries.description: dbt Labs' MCP server gives agents context on your dbt Core, Fusion or Platform project: models, lineage, tests, Semantic Layer metrics, and the ability to run dbt commands. Useful for analytics engineering with an agent. Run via uvx with env config, or import the experimental MCP bundle.
entries.use_case: Ask the agent which downstream models break if you change a column, using dbt lineage, then run the affected tests.
entries.safety_notes: Official; scope dbt Platform tokens
entries.accounts_needed: dbt project; dbt Platform token optional

entries.name: planning-with-files
entries.author: Ahmad Othman
entries.description: A planning skill that keeps the plan on disk and fires a hook every turn so the agent can't forget it, surviving /clear and context resets. Useful for long tasks. Install with `npx skills add OthmanAdi/planning-with-files --skill planning-with-files -g`.
entries.use_case: On a long refactor, keep the plan in a file that a hook re-reads each turn so the agent stays on track after /clear.
entries.safety_notes: Clean scan, but it adds many hooks that run every session; read them first

entries.name: UI/UX Pro Max
entries.author: NextLevelBuilder
entries.description: A design-intelligence skill with searchable style, color, typography and UX rule databases that agents consult when building UI across many frameworks. Can improve generic-looking UIs. Install via the Claude marketplace (`/plugin install ui-ux-pro-max@ui-ux-pro-max-skill`).
entries.use_case: When a generated landing page looks generic, have the agent pick a style, palette and typography from the skill's databases and restyle it.
entries.safety_notes: Clean scan, but the org was created the same day as the repo and the star count looks out of line with its following

entries.name: Expo skills
entries.author: Expo
entries.description: Expo's official skills for building, deploying, upgrading and debugging Expo and React Native apps, including EAS workflows. Useful only if you ship mobile apps with Expo. Install with `npx skills add expo/skills` or the Claude plugin directory.
entries.use_case: Have the agent upgrade an Expo app to the latest SDK and set up an EAS build workflow.
entries.safety_notes: Official; docs-only

entries.name: Firebase agent skills
entries.author: Firebase
entries.description: Official Agent Skills for Firebase: Auth, Firestore, Hosting, Analytics instrumentation and more. Copy them into your skills folder or install with a skills CLI when building on Firebase.
entries.use_case: Have the agent set up Firebase Auth and Firestore security rules correctly for a new app.
entries.safety_notes: Official Firebase; docs-only skills; 'analytics' hits are Firebase Analytics how-tos, not telemetry

entries.name: Google Workspace CLI
entries.author: Google Workspace
entries.description: `gws`, one CLI for every Google Workspace API (Drive, Gmail, Calendar and more), built from Google's Discovery Service at runtime and shipped with 40+ agent skills. It returns structured JSON, which suits agents. Install with `npm install -g @googleworkspace/cli`; the repo notes it is not an officially supported Google product.
entries.use_case: Let the agent find this week's meeting notes in Drive and email a summary through Gmail, getting structured JSON back from each call.
entries.safety_notes: Official; npm postinstall fetches a binary and the CLI asks for broad Google scopes

entries.name: Kubernetes MCP Server
entries.author: Marc Nuri (Red Hat) / containers org
entries.description: A Go MCP server that lets agents inspect and manage any Kubernetes or OpenShift resource, pods, logs, events and Helm releases, reading your kubeconfig directly with no kubectl needed. Useful for infra debugging. Run with `npx kubernetes-mcp-server@latest`, ideally with `--read-only`.
entries.use_case: When a pod keeps crash-looping, have the agent pull its logs and events and explain the failure.
entries.safety_notes: Legit (creator is a Red Hat principal engineer), but it can change live clusters; use its read-only and disable-destructive flags

entries.name: pstack-claude
entries.author: Michael Denyer
entries.description: A port of pstack for Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Copilot and Muse that tracks upstream and carries declared policy forks and hooks. For people who want pstack in Claude with extra glue. Install via its Claude marketplace; prefer the official source.
entries.use_case: Use pstack's skills in Claude Code with extra hooks if you don't run Cursor.
entries.safety_notes: Unofficial copy with hooks; prefer the official source
entries.related_note: Unofficial port of pstack with policy forks

entries.name: Supabase MCP
entries.author: Supabase
entries.description: Supabase's MCP server that lets agents manage tables, query data, run migrations and fetch config for your Supabase projects. It documents a read-only, project-scoped mode. Connect via the hosted URL or npx, after reading its security guidance.
entries.use_case: Let the agent create a table and run a migration on a development Supabase project, scoped read-only on production.
entries.safety_notes: Official, but it can change your database; use the read_only and project-scoped mode it documents

entries.name: Symphony
entries.author: OpenAI
entries.description: Symphony watches a Linear board and spawns isolated, autonomous coding-agent runs per issue, each returning proof of work such as CI results and PRs. It is OpenAI's reference for 'harness engineering' at team scale. Clone it, set Linear and model keys, and run it in a trusted environment.
entries.use_case: Have each new Linear issue start an isolated agent run that returns CI results and a PR, in a trusted test environment.
entries.safety_notes: Official OpenAI, but the README calls it an engineering preview for trusted environments; needs LINEAR_API_KEY and autonomous agents act on your repos

entries.name: Claude Code Security Review
entries.author: Anthropic
entries.description: A GitHub Action that uses Claude Code to review PR diffs for security vulnerabilities and comment on the PR. Easy security coverage for every PR. Add the action to a workflow with an Anthropic API key; run it only on trusted PRs.
entries.use_case: On every trusted PR, have Claude comment on injection, auth and secrets issues in the diff before human review.
entries.safety_notes: Official, but its README says it isn't hardened against prompt injection; run only on trusted PRs

entries.name: Episodic Memory
entries.author: Jesse Vincent
entries.description: Indexes your past Claude Code conversations locally in SQLite with vectors, so agents can semantically search earlier sessions for decisions and fixes. It pairs with Superpowers. Install as a Claude Code plugin or via npm.
entries.use_case: Ask "how did we fix the auth timeout last month?" and let the agent search your past Claude Code sessions locally.
entries.safety_notes: Trusted author (Superpowers). npm postinstall runs a local script to rebuild the native SQLite binding; summarization bills ANTHROPIC_API_KEY if set

entries.name: Purple Llama
entries.author: Meta
entries.description: Meta's umbrella project for LLM safety: Llama Guard and Prompt Guard classifiers, Code Shield and the CyberSecEval benchmarks. Useful if you need input/output filtering or security benchmarks. Components install separately via their own instructions.
entries.use_case: Filter user input and model output through Llama Guard in your chat product to block unsafe content.
entries.safety_notes: Official Meta; hits are benchmark attack prompts
entries.install: Per component (e.g. Llama Guard weights from Hugging Face)
entries.accounts_needed: Hugging Face access to the models

entries.name: W&B skills
entries.author: Weights & Biases
entries.description: Official Agent Skills for W&B Models and Weave tracing and evals. Install with the repo's script or copy the skills when your agent works with W&B.
entries.use_case: Have the agent instrument a model training script with W&B and set up Weave evals.
entries.safety_notes: Official W&B; install.sh only copies skills and prints WANDB_API_KEY instructions; 'yolo' hits are YOLOv5 model names

entries.name: Agent Plugins for AWS
entries.author: AWS Labs
entries.description: Plugins and skills from AWS Labs that teach coding agents to architect, deploy and operate specific AWS services (serverless, Amplify, Location, Transform, SageMaker HyperPod). Install the plugins you need into Claude Code or Codex.
entries.use_case: Have the agent set up an Amplify app or a serverless backend following AWS's service-specific skills.
entries.safety_notes: Official AWS Labs. The aws-transform skill tells the agent to run an AWS-hosted curl ... | bash installer; SageMaker diagnostic scripts pipe base64-decoded commands to bash on remote nodes by design; needs AWS credentials

entries.name: pstack port (backnotprop)
entries.author: backnotprop
entries.description: A standalone mirror of Cursor's pstack (Lauren Tan's skills) kept in sync for people who don't use Cursor, installable into Claude Code, Codex, Pi and others. Same content as the official plugin, one hop removed. Install with `npx skills add backnotprop/pstack`; prefer cursor/plugins when you can.
entries.use_case: Install pstack's skills into Claude Code or Codex if you want them outside Cursor.
entries.safety_notes: Unofficial copy; use Cursor's official pstack instead
entries.related_note: Mirror of pstack in cursor/plugins (same SKILL.md files)

entries.name: Taste Skill
entries.author: Leon Lin
entries.description: Taste Skill gives coding agents art direction for company websites: pick one of several design directions, use one design system and real photos, then check the page in a browser at several widths before finishing. Pages take a while and many tokens. Install with `npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill --skill design-taste-frontend`.
entries.use_case: Have the agent build a company website in one consistent design direction and check it at several screen widths before calling it done.
entries.safety_notes: Clean scan and a real creator (33k X followers), but 112k stars in 9 months for one skill is far above peers

entries.name: AI-Infra-Guard
entries.author: Tencent
entries.description: Tencent Zhuque Lab's A.I.G platform for AI red teaming: agent and skill scanning, MCP and AI-infrastructure vulnerability scanning and jailbreak evaluation. Broad, with live attack payloads. Install via pip packages like `aig-infra-scan` or the full platform, ideally in a sandbox.
entries.use_case: Scan your AI infrastructure and MCP servers for known vulnerabilities and run jailbreak evaluations from one dashboard, in a sandbox.
entries.safety_notes: Official Tencent, but it ships live attack payloads; run it in a sandbox
entries.ease_note: Platform deploy or pip; run sandboxed

entries.name: Awesome Copilot
entries.author: GitHub
entries.description: GitHub's community collection of Copilot custom agents, instructions, skills, hooks and workflows, with a searchable website and an llms.txt for agents. Good for finding prompt and instruction ideas, even outside Copilot. Browse awesome-copilot.github.com and copy what you need.
entries.use_case: Find a ready-made custom instruction or agent for code review and adapt it to your own harness.
entries.safety_notes: Official repo but community-contributed (478 skills); has a submission gate, still read each one

entries.name: Neon skills
entries.author: Neon
entries.description: Neon's skills and integrations for its serverless Postgres (branching, connection setup, migrations). Useful if your database runs on Neon. Install with `npx skills add neondatabase/agent-skills` or the Claude marketplace.
entries.use_case: Have the agent create a Neon branch to test a migration before running it on the main database.
entries.safety_notes: Official; small and docs-only

entries.name: Claude Skills (Rezvani)
entries.author: Alireza Rezvani
entries.description: A collection of 411 skills and plugins for Claude Code and 12 other agents, grouped into bundles (engineering, product, marketing, compliance, finance, executive), with published tests of whether each skill loads on plain-language prompts. Useful to cherry-pick role skills. Install a bundle with `/plugin install engineering-skills@claude-code-skills`.
entries.use_case: Install only the product or compliance bundle when a non-engineering task, such as a PRD or a SOC 2 checklist, comes up.
entries.safety_notes: Large single-maintainer set; scan hits were its own security-auditor examples, but read before bulk install

entries.name: Claude Subconscious
entries.author: Letta
entries.description: Hooks that send each Claude Code transcript to a Letta agent, which studies your codebase and the web and 'whispers back' memory before your next prompt. It is an experiment in background memory for coding agents. Install the hooks and set a Letta key.
entries.use_case: Experiment with a background agent that learns your codebase from Claude Code transcripts (self-host Letta first).
entries.safety_notes: Ships every Claude Code session transcript to Letta cloud by default (set LETTA_BASE_URL to self-host); a background agent reads files and searches the web
entries.accounts_needed: Letta API key or self-hosted Letta

entries.name: OpenClaw
entries.author: Peter Steinberger (@steipete) and community
entries.description: OpenClaw is an open-source personal AI assistant that runs on your machine and meets you in 20+ chat apps (Slack, Telegram, WhatsApp and others), with swappable model plugins and local memory. It has broad system access by design. Install with its shell script or npm.
entries.use_case: Message a personal assistant on Telegram to check your calendar and draft replies, running on a machine you control and isolate.
entries.safety_notes: Clean core, but it gets broad system access and its skill marketplace has had malware

entries.name: Antigravity CLI
entries.author: Google (Antigravity)
entries.description: `agy` is the terminal surface of Google's Antigravity 2.0 agent harness. It asks before edits and commands by default, and its auto mode runs commands inside an OS sandbox. Install with the curl script from the README; there is no source here.
entries.use_case: Try Google's Antigravity agent from the terminal, asking before each edit, while comparing it with Gemini CLI.
entries.safety_notes: Official Google, but no LICENSE file (README and changelog only; the binary installs via curl). README: Interactions data is collected by default, opt out in settings. Default mode asks before edits and commands; auto mode sandboxes commands; --dangerously-skip-permissions exists
entries.related_note: Same vendor as Gemini CLI; closed binary

entries.name: AWS MCP Servers
entries.author: AWS
entries.description: AWS Labs' suite of specialized MCP servers for AWS services (docs, CDK, cost, EKS, Lambda and many more), now succeeded by the Agent Toolkit for AWS. Use it if you run on AWS. Each server runs via `uvx`.
entries.use_case: Have the agent estimate the monthly cost of a CDK stack with the AWS cost server (prefer the Agent Toolkit for new setups).
entries.safety_notes: Official AWS; uses your AWS credentials, so give it a limited role

quality_breakdown.quality_cap_reason: Superseded by Agent Toolkit for AWS

entries.name: Browserbase skills
entries.author: Browserbase
entries.description: Browserbase's skills that let Claude Code drive remote cloud browsers through the official `browse` CLI, with identity, CAPTCHA solving, proxies, traces and serverless browser functions. Good when local browsers aren't enough. Install via the Claude marketplace or `npx skills add browserbase/skills`; needs a Browserbase account.
entries.use_case: When a site blocks headless local browsers, have the agent drive a remote cloud browser with proxies and CAPTCHA handling.
entries.safety_notes: Official; one skill reads its API key from your keychain or 1Password

entries.name: Obsidian skills
entries.author: Steph Ango (@kepano), Obsidian CEO
entries.description: Skills from Obsidian's CEO that teach agents Obsidian's formats: Markdown flavors, Bases, JSON Canvas and the Obsidian CLI. Useful if your notes, specs or knowledge base live in an Obsidian vault. Install as a Claude marketplace plugin or with `npx skills add`.
entries.use_case: Have the agent build an Obsidian Base that tracks your product specs by status.
entries.safety_notes: Small docs-only set from Obsidian's CEO

entries.name: tstack
entries.author: Theo Browne (@theo)
entries.description: Theo Browne's personal agent skills, cleaned up for Claude Code and Codex. Highlights are full-send (prove, review, file, babysit and merge a PR unattended), council (three models from different providers review until they agree) and loop-style reviewers. Best for people who want aggressive PR automation; install with the skills CLI or copy the folders.
entries.use_case: Hand a small PR to full-send so it proves, reviews and merges it, or ask council for a three-model review on a risky change.
entries.safety_notes: Clean scan, but full-send merges PRs and force-pushes its own branch unattended
entries.ease_note: Copy or skills CLI; some skills prefer T3 Code features

entries.name: Scientific Agent Skills
entries.author: K-Dense AI
entries.description: 177 skills for scientific work: bioinformatics, chemistry, scientific databases, data analysis and literature research, from the K-Dense startup. Valuable for research-heavy tasks, not general product work. Install with `npx skills add K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills`.
entries.use_case: Have the agent pull protein data from a public database and run a sequence analysis for a research question.
entries.safety_notes: Startup-run, not a lab; some skills point at third-party install scripts
entries.ease_note: npx; some skills need extra installs

entries.name: Trail of Bits Claude Code config
entries.author: Trail of Bits
entries.description: Trail of Bits' opinionated Claude Code defaults: permission deny rules for SSH keys and cloud credentials, sandboxing, hooks, local-model setup and workflows. Read it as a hardening reference and copy the parts you want into your settings.
entries.use_case: Copy its deny rules so Claude Code can never read your SSH keys or cloud credentials.
entries.safety_notes: Strong credential deny rules for ~/.ssh and cloud credentials, BUT it recommends a `claude-yolo` alias (--dangerously-skip-permissions) inside its sandbox and uses rustup and LM Studio curl|sh installers. No LICENSE

entries.name: Atlassian MCP Server
entries.author: Atlassian
entries.description: Atlassian's official cloud-hosted MCP server for Jira, Confluence, JSM, Bitbucket, Compass and Loom, OAuth-scoped to your site. Useful if your team tracks work in Jira. Add with `claude mcp add --transport http atlassian https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp`.
entries.use_case: Ask the agent to summarize all open Jira tickets for a release and update their Confluence release notes.
entries.safety_notes: Official; OAuth-scoped
entries.install: claude mcp add --transport http atlassian https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp

entries.name: Awesome MCP Servers
entries.author: Frank Fiegel (punkpeye)
entries.description: A large community list of MCP servers grouped by category, maintained by the founder of the Glama MCP directory. Good for discovering servers; every entry is third-party and unvetted. Browse the README or glama.ai.
entries.use_case: Search the list for a calendar or CRM MCP server, then vet the one you pick before installing.
entries.safety_notes: A list; entries are third-party and unvetted

entries.name: Azure Skills plugin
entries.author: Microsoft
entries.description: Microsoft's Azure plugin that bundles curated Azure skills with MCP-backed execution, so an agent can choose services, validate and deploy real resources. Aimed at teams shipping on Azure. Install via the Claude marketplace (`/plugin install azure@azure-skills`).
entries.use_case: Have the agent choose the right Azure service for a new API, validate the config and deploy it.
entries.safety_notes: Official, but skills create real cloud resources; review plans before approving
entries.related_note: Shares 54 identical SKILL.md files with microsoft/skills

entries.name: Cline Skills
entries.author: Cline
entries.description: The skills Cline's own team uses, in SKILL.md format (for example Railway deploy and database analysis). Cline installs skills through `npx skills`, so these also work in other harnesses.
entries.use_case: Use Cline's Railway deploy skill to have any agent ship a service to Railway.
entries.safety_notes: Official Cline org; hits are Railway SSH how-to docs. Small and young (45 stars)

entries.name: n8n Skills
entries.author: Romuald Czlonkowski
entries.description: Fourteen Claude Code skills plus a router skill and hooks that teach agents to build production-ready n8n workflows with n8n-MCP and deploy self-hosted n8n. Companion to n8n-MCP. Install with `/plugin marketplace add czlonkowski/n8n-skills`.
entries.use_case: Pair with n8n-MCP so the agent follows n8n's expression syntax and validation rules when building workflows.
entries.safety_notes: Clean scan; hooks only enforce its own rules

entries.name: Remotion skills
entries.author: Remotion
entries.description: Remotion's skills for making videos with code: one best-practices skill that covers compositions, animation, audio and rendering. Handy for product demo or launch videos generated by an agent. Install with `npx skills add remotion-dev/skills`; Remotion's own license terms apply.
entries.use_case: Have the agent write a 30-second product demo video in React with Remotion and render it to MP4.
entries.safety_notes: Official; docs-only (Remotion's own license terms apply)

entries.name: Amplifier
entries.author: Microsoft
entries.description: Amplifier is a Microsoft research demonstrator: a modular AI development assistant built from composable modules and agents, successor to the earlier Claude Code-based Amplifier. It is for exploring harness design rather than daily use. Install with uv per the README.
entries.use_case: Explore how a modular AI assistant composes agents and tools, as research for your own harness design.
entries.safety_notes: Official Microsoft, but the README cautions it is a research demonstrator with permissive AI tools; installer path uses astral uv curl|sh / irm|iex

entries.name: Gemini skills
entries.author: Google (Gemini)
entries.description: Agent Skills from Google for building with the Gemini API and SDKs: model selection, interactions and agent patterns, in the standard SKILL.md format. Copy them into your agent's skills folder or install with a skills CLI.
entries.use_case: Have the agent pick the right Gemini model and write correct SDK code for a new feature.
entries.safety_notes: Official Google Gemini org. The gemini-api-cli skill tells the agent to run a curl ... install.sh | bash installer from raw.githubusercontent.com; reads the Gemini API key from env
entries.accounts_needed: Gemini API key for real calls

entries.name: React Native skills
entries.author: Callstack
entries.description: Callstack's React Native skills in three bundles: building (performance, navigation, upgrades), testing (CI artifacts, device automation, exploratory QA) and migrating to RN. Drawn from a major RN consultancy's production work. Install with `npx skills add callstackincubator/agent-skills`.
entries.use_case: Have the agent profile and fix a janky list screen in a React Native app using Callstack's performance skills.
entries.safety_notes: Known RN consultancy; docs-only

entries.name: Awesome Agent Skills
entries.author: VoltAgent
entries.description: VoltAgent's collection of official skills from engineering teams plus community picks, compatible with most coding agents, and it says it avoids bulk AI-generated entries. One of the better-curated lists. Browse the README and install entries with their own commands.
entries.use_case: Find an official skill from a vendor you already use, such as a database or payments company, before reaching for a community one.
entries.safety_notes: A list; entries unvetted

entries.name: NVIDIA skills
entries.author: NVIDIA
entries.description: NVIDIA's verified skills catalog for CUDA-X, robotics and simulation, RAG blueprints and platform tools, mirrored daily from product repos. Mainly for GPU and Physical AI work. Start with the nvidia-skill-finder skill via `npx skills add nvidia/skills`.
entries.use_case: Ask the nvidia-skill-finder which skill to use for a CUDA or RAG blueprint task, then install only that one.
entries.safety_notes: Official, but huge; some skills run vendor install scripts and set up SSH keys for clusters

entries.name: Agent Skills Discovery RFC
entries.author: Cloudflare
entries.description: A draft RFC for publishing Agent Skills at a /.well-known/ URL so agents can discover a site's skills, with an index, integrity checks and archive distribution. It is a spec, not a tool. Read it if you plan to publish skills for your own product.
entries.use_case: If you publish skills for your own product, follow the RFC to serve them at a /.well-known/ URL agents can discover.
entries.safety_notes: Spec text only

entries.name: Awesome Claude Code
entries.author: hesreallyhim
entries.description: A hand-picked list of Claude Code resources: skills, agents, status lines, hooks, tooling and plugins, with an emphasis on quality and originality. Good for finding small useful tools like ccusage. Browse the README.
entries.use_case: Find a status line, hook or small tool for Claude Code that someone has already built and reviewed.
entries.safety_notes: A list; entries unvetted

entries.name: Codex Skills Catalog
entries.author: OpenAI
entries.description: OpenAI's original Codex skills catalog, now marked deprecated in favor of the OpenAI Plugins repository. Still a readable set of examples for how Codex packages skills. For new work, follow OpenAI's Build plugins guide instead.
entries.use_case: Read an example to see how Codex packages a skill, then build new ones as OpenAI plugins instead.
entries.safety_notes: Official; a few skills install vendor CLIs from their official URLs. README: deprecated, use openai/plugins.

entries.name: Ruflo (Claude Flow)
entries.author: Reuven Cohen (ruvnet)
entries.description: Ruflo is an agent meta-harness for Claude Code and Codex that adds swarms of agents, hooks, memory and an MCP server to a project via `npx ruflo@latest init`. Ambitious, with a very large surface. Read its hooks and postinstall before using.
entries.use_case: Experiment with agent swarms on a throwaway repo after reading every hook and postinstall script it adds.
entries.safety_notes: Its npm postinstall patches other packages in node_modules; very large hook surface

entries.name: TDD Guard
entries.author: Nizar Selander
entries.description: TDD Guard uses Claude Code hooks to enforce test-driven development: it blocks writing implementation without a failing test and explains what to do instead. The author's newer Probity tool extends this to Codex and Copilot. Install with `/plugin marketplace add nizos/tdd-guard` and a test reporter.
entries.use_case: Stop Claude Code from writing implementation code until a failing test exists for it.
entries.safety_notes: Clean scan; hooks only check test state

entries.name: Awesome Claude Skills (Composio)
entries.author: Composio
entries.description: Composio's list of 1000+ Claude skills and plugins for Claude, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and more, which also promotes Composio's MCP gateway. Use it to find skills, then vet each one. Browse the README.
entries.use_case: Look for a skill idea, then install it from its original author's repo after vetting it.
entries.safety_notes: Vendor-run list that also promotes Composio; vet each entry
entries.related_note: Re-bundles copies of official Anthropic skills

entries.name: Notion MCP Server
entries.author: Notion
entries.description: Notion's self-hosted MCP server; the README now says it is no longer actively maintained and recommends Notion's hosted Remote MCP instead. Kept here as reference. Use the remote server for new setups.
entries.use_case: Only as reference: for new setups, connect Notion's hosted MCP so the agent can search and update your workspace.
entries.safety_notes: Official; use a token scoped to the pages it needs
entries.related_note: Unmaintained; Notion recommends its hosted MCP

entries.name: Agentic Awesome Skills
entries.author: sickn33 (Nick)
entries.description: A library of nearly 3,000 SKILL.md playbooks for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI, with 'AAS Core' to search the catalog and preview a plan before installing. The breadth is the selling point, but quality and provenance vary widely. Install with `npx agentic-awesome-skills --<agent>`; if you use it, copy single skills you have read.
entries.use_case: Search the catalog for a niche skill and preview its plan, then copy just that skill after reading it line by line.
entries.safety_notes: Huge unvetted bulk set incl. offensive pentest payloads; maintainer's GitHub bio carries a pump.fun token address
entries.ease_note: npx installer; must vet each skill

entries.name: Amp Official Plugins
entries.author: Amp
entries.description: Official plugins and skills for Amp's agent mode, such as building scheduled runs. Amp is a closed-source agent CLI and IDE extension spun out of Sourcegraph, and it also loads `.claude/skills` natively. Install plugins from inside Amp.
entries.use_case: In Amp, add the scheduled-runs plugin to have the agent run a maintenance task on a timer.
entries.safety_notes: Official Amp org, but no LICENSE. Amp itself defaults to allow-all permissions when none are configured and allows MCP servers that match no rule (cited from search, not fetched directly); threads sync to ampcode.com; auto-updates are on

entries.name: Claude for Financial Services
entries.author: Anthropic
entries.description: Claude Code plugins, skills and managed-agent cookbooks for finance work such as IC memos, earnings reviews and GL reconciliation, plus partner MCP connectors. It is for finance teams; install the plugins from the marketplace.
entries.use_case: Have Claude draft an investment-committee memo from a company's filings using the financial-analysis plugin.
entries.safety_notes: Official Anthropic; partner plugins connect to external financial-data MCP endpoints (LSEG, PitchBook, FactSet) and deploy scripts need ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Scan otherwise clean

entries.name: Continue
entries.author: Continue
entries.description: Continue is an open-source coding agent and assistant for VS Code and JetBrains with configurable models, rules and MCP tools. Its status changed in mid-2026, so treat it as a watch item. Install the extension from the marketplace.
entries.use_case: Configure your own models, rules and MCP tools for in-editor chat and edits (watch its project status).
entries.safety_notes: Large Apache-2.0 project, but its last commit (21 Jul 2026) says the login flow was retired after an acquisition; ownership and future are unclear. Don't adopt until that is clarified
entries.install: Install the VS Code or JetBrains extension

entries.name: Vibe Kanban
entries.author: Bloop AI
entries.description: Vibe Kanban lets you plan work as kanban issues, then start Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI or other agents in isolated workspaces per issue and review their diffs. The README now announces it is sunsetting. Run with `npx vibe-kanban`.
entries.use_case: Create kanban cards for five small fixes and start an agent per card in isolated workspaces, reviewing each diff (note: it is sunsetting).
entries.safety_notes: Clean scan, but the README says the project is sunsetting

entries.name: Awesome Claude Skills (travisvn)
entries.author: Travis VN
entries.description: A curated list of Claude Skills with a clear explainer of how skills load (progressive disclosure) and pointers to official and community packs. Good orientation for newcomers. Browse the README.
entries.use_case: Read the explainer on how skills load, then follow its links to the official packs.
entries.safety_notes: A list; last updated Apr 2026

entries.name: ClawHub community skills
entries.author: OpenClaw
entries.description: ClawHub is OpenClaw's public skill registry for publishing, versioning and searching SKILL.md packages and plugins. Security researchers found hundreds of malicious skills uploaded there. Don't install third-party skills from it.
entries.use_case: None recommended: don't install third-party skills from it; use vendor marketplaces instead.
entries.safety_notes: Snyk, Acronis and Palo Alto Unit 42 found hundreds of malicious skills uploaded there; don't install its third-party skills unreviewed
